chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Uqba ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) judged that the fruits of the palm tree belong to the one who pollinated it, unless the buyer stipulates otherwise.
ai.seo_question: Who owns the fruit of a palm tree after sale according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the default ownership of palm fruit in commercial transactions, attributing it to the pollinator (usually the seller) unless explicitly stipulated otherwise. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on contractual freedom and the precise allocation of produce based on labor and care, a principle widely cited in fiqh discussions regarding agricultural sales.
